claims.text: A female patient aged 13 years with neural tube defects, VP-shunt, neurogenic bladder, chronic renal insufficiency and hypertension on intermittent catheterization and prophylactic antibiotics presented with fever, vomiting and malodorous urine; a first Morganella morganii urinary tract infection was managed as an outpatient. Imaging showed an atrophic left kidney, a hydronephrotic right kidney, a trabeculated bladder and grade III right vesicoureteral reflux. A second M. morganii infection occurred at age 16 years; she was an inpatient, treated with meropenem and teicoplanin before culture and meropenem after culture, continued for 20 days because of persistent pyuria.

claims.text: A male patient aged 16 years with a neural tube defect and neurogenic bladder on intermittent catheterization with a DJ catheter presented as an outpatient with flank pain and recurrent UTI. M. morganii was isolated; ultrasound showed a left-sided obstructed, atrophied kidney and a MAG-3 scan showed impaired function. Cefuroxime was given after culture; duration was not documented.

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

claims.text: A male patient aged 2 years with a neural tube defect, ventriculoatrial shunt and neurogenic bladder on intermittent catheterization presented with fever, vomiting, decreased activity and malodorous turbid urine. He was an inpatient with CRP 26.9 mg/L, bilateral hydronephrosis and negative blood and CSF cultures, and received ceftriaxone for 10 days.

evidence.quote: 3 | 2 years | M | Fever, vomiting, decreased activity, malodorous turbid urine | None | Neural tube defect, ventriculoatrial shunt, neurogenic bladder | No | Intermittent catheterization | No
3 | Inpatient | Ceftriaxone | Ceftriaxone | 10 days
of which 9 (1.1%) were attributed to Morganella infection
Patient | Inpatient vs. outpatient | Treatment prior to culture | Treatment after culture | Duration of treatment

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

claims.text: A female patient aged 1 year 9 months with a neural tube defect, VP-shunt and vesicoureteral reflux on intermittent catheterization, a DJ catheter and prophylactic antibiotics presented with fever, irritability and malodorous urine. Ultrasound showed normal kidneys and a trabeculated bladder with grade II left and grade I right reflux. She received ertapenem before culture and cefixime afterwards for 10 days.

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

claims.text: A female patient aged 2 years with vesicoureteral reflux and recurrent UTI on prophylactic antibiotics presented with fever, hypoactivity, malodorous turbid urine and dysuria. Leukocyte count was 20.8 x10^3/mm^3 with bilateral moderate hydronephrosis and negative blood culture. Ertapenem was given for 10 days as an inpatient.

evidence.quote: 5 | 2 years | F | Fever, hypoactivity, malodorous turbid urine, dysuria | Prophylactic antibiotics | VUR | Yes | None | Yes
5 | Inpatient | Ertapenem | Ertapenem | 10 days
of which 9 (1.1%) were attributed to Morganella infection
Patient | Inpatient vs. outpatient | Treatment prior to culture | Treatment after culture | Duration of treatment

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

claims.text: A female patient aged 4 years 7 months with neurogenic bladder and recurrent UTI on prophylactic antibiotics and solifenacin presented with abdominal pain, dysuria, frequency and urgency. Ultrasound showed a thickened bladder wall and other imaging showed no reflux. Nitrofurantoin was given before culture, then meropenem followed by cefixime for 10 days.

of which 9 (1.1%) were attributed to Morganella infection

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

claims.text: A female patient aged 16 years with respiratory failure and recurrent UTI developed an infection in hospital with abdominal pain. Ultrasound showed no abnormalities. Levofloxacin was given before culture and piperacillin-tazobactam afterwards for 14 days.

of which 9 (1.1%) were attributed to Morganella infection

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

claims.text: A female patient aged 2 years without comorbidity presented with fever, vomiting and abdominal pain. Urinalysis showed no bacteriuria, ultrasound was normal and blood and CSF cultures were negative. Vancomycin was given before culture, then ceftriaxone, imipenem and ciprofloxacin for 10 days.

evidence.quote: 8 | 2 years | F | Fever, vomiting, abdominal pain | None | None | No | None | No
8 | Inpatient → outpatient | Vancomycin | Ceftriaxone → imipenem → ciprofloxacin | 10 days
of which 9 (1.1%) were attributed to Morganella infection
Patient | Inpatient vs. outpatient | Treatment prior to culture | Treatment after culture | Duration of treatment

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.

limitations: The source has no captions for its five unwrapped graphics; figure attribution relies on matching content to Tables 1 to 4 and pixels are described only in the visual submission.
Vomiting is reported in 2 patients (22.2%) in the text but Table 1 lists vomiting for three patients; both are kept and no cohort count is copied to individuals.

The text says recurrent UTIs occurred in five patients, four of whom were on prophylactic antibiotics and performed intermittent catheterization, which does not match Table 1 (five recurrent; prophylaxis in four patients, only some of them recurrent, intermittent catheterization in four patients). Table values are used.
Seven patients are said to have required inpatient management, whereas Table 3 lists inpatient care for eight patients across nine rows including a second episode of patient 1.
The graphical abstract prints 78.8% female while the text gives 77.8%; the figure is aggregate and not used for facts.
The text lists myelomeningocele in 44% but Table 1 says neural tube defect; the terms are not equated for individual patients.

Table 2 lists other cultures as None for patients 1, 2, 6, 7 and 9 while the text says blood cultures remained negative across all cases; for those patients the negative blood culture is kept review-only.
Which one of nine UTIs was not a lower UTI is not stated; no upper or lower tract classification is assigned to individuals.
Table 2 gives no unit or method for urine white and red cell counts; text values are kept as printed. Same as above for patient 1 second episode refers to the first-episode imaging row.

Susceptibility results in Table 4 are isolate-level aggregates and are not attributed to individual patients except that both isolates of patient 1 were similar. Treatment duration in Table 3 is given once per row; it is kept on the drug only when the same single drug was given before and after culture, otherwise only in the regimen text.
Positive treatment response in inpatients is a cohort-level statement and is not copied to individual patients; no outcomes beyond patient 1 second infection are documented individually.
